We’re a Toronto-based team participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026! 🚀

Our team brings experience in software engineering, AI/ML, cloud computing, and geospatial data analysis. 

We're looking for passionate teammates with skills in Python, GIS, Earth science, satellite data, data visualization, UI/UX, and full-stack development.

Join us to build something innovative, scientifically meaningful, and impactful, with the goal of competing for NASA Space Apps awards!
summary:
Parallax BLINDSPOT is an interactive satellite intelligence platform developed by Parallax Labs for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026: Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots.

NASA's MODIS and VIIRS sensors detect thermal activity from space, but their observations can differ across locations and dates. Traditional hotspot maps show detections without making these differences easy to investigate.

BLINDSPOT harmonizes NASA FIRMS observations using a common 10-kilometre Equal Earth grid and UTC day. Through interactive maps, Satellite Blindspot Reveal, a historical calendar, and an immersive Observatory, users can explore where sensor records overlap and differ.

We processed 20.66 million worldwide NASA source observations and preserved a detailed Alberta 2023 case study. In Alberta, 45.8% of active grid-days contained observations from only one sensor family.

Our goal is to make satellite evidence more transparent and useful for researchers, environmental analysts, and wildfire preparedness teams. BLINDSPOT supports investigation not verified fire detection accuracy or future-fire prediction.
details:
The Problem

Imagine Maya, a wildfire preparedness analyst, trying to understand historical fire activity. She compares NASA MODIS and VIIRS observations of the same region and discovers that the datasets do not always agree.

MODIS and VIIRS have different observation characteristics, including spatial resolution, sensitivity, and satellite overpass timing. Comparing raw hotspot counts can therefore produce misleading interpretations. Analysts need a consistent way to investigate both the agreements and differences between these records.

Our Solution

Parallax BLINDSPOT transforms complex satellite observations into an interactive, explainable investigation experience.

The application provides:

  • Satellite Blindspot Reveal: Synchronized maps and a draggable comparison slider that distinguish MODIS-only, VIIRS-only, and shared observations.
  • Historical Fire Calendar: Month-by-month exploration of satellite-observed thermal activity.
  • World Atlas: Geographic exploration of NASA observations across multiple regions.
  • Interactive Observatory: A story-driven introduction designed to make the scientific problem understandable to nontechnical users.
  • Evidence and Readiness Briefs: Summaries of observed patterns, data provenance, and questions requiring further investigation.
  • Watchtower: Optional recent hotspot monitoring through NASA FIRMS when configured with an API key.

How It Works

We obtained authentic NASA FIRMS MODIS Collection 6.1 and VIIRS Suomi-NPP Collection 2 observations.

Our Python data pipeline standardizes the observations spatially using a 10-kilometre Equal Earth projected grid (EPSG:8857) and temporally using UTC calendar days.

For each grid cell and day, the system identifies whether MODIS, VIIRS, or both recorded thermal activity. These results are stored in SQLite for interactive exploration.

We keep standard-processing data and provisional near-real-time observations distinguishable, exclude identified nonvegetation thermal sources from applicable standard-processing comparisons, and preserve source provenance.

Results and Evidence

We processed 20,659,624 worldwide NASA source observations, with 19,573,939 eligible under our processing rules, into 5,708,602 distinct worldwide 10-km grid-days. The global archive covers portions of November 2025 through November 2026.

We also preserved a detailed Alberta, Canada, case study containing 547,021 original observations from May–October 2023.

In Alberta, our analysis identified 17,094 active grid-days:

  • 9,268 recorded by both sensor families
  • 1,084 recorded by MODIS only
  • 6,742 recorded by VIIRS only

That means 45.8% of active grid-days contained records from just one sensor family. This is a measure of observational overlap, not proof that a satellite missed a fire.

Technology

BLINDSPOT uses Python, FastAPI, SQLite, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Leaflet, and interactive globe visualization. The application combines reproducible geospatial processing with responsive mapping and evidence-based storytelling.

Innovation and Impact

Our innovation is not another wildfire hotspot map. BLINDSPOT makes differences between satellite observation records visible and explorable.

Researchers can investigate sensor disagreement. Environmental analysts can explore seasonal patterns. Wildfire preparedness teams can identify observations that deserve further verification.

The indexed data architecture supports expanding the analysis across additional locations, time periods, and datasets without replacing the core workflow.

Limitations and Future Development

Satellite thermal anomalies are not necessarily confirmed wildfire incidents.

Our current global dataset covers roughly one year, not a validated multi-decade baseline. Our comparison does not correct for every difference in sensor sensitivity, cloud cover, or observation timing.

BLINDSPOT does not currently provide validated future wildfire ignition predictions or official emergency alerts.

Future work includes more historical satellite observations, independent agency validation, vegetation and atmospheric data integration, and rigorously evaluated forecasting models.

Our mission: We do not make satellites agree. We make their differences useful.

Developed by Asma Ahmed and Ayaan Ahmed - Parallax Labs.
